scenario.prompt_to_agent:
The user on pc1 (195.11.14.2) reports they cannot reach pc2
(200.1.1.2) or anything outside their own subnet since "cleaning
up" their network settings -- their pings now fail with
"Destination Host Unreachable". Oddly, pc1 pings its gateway
195.11.14.1 fine. The partner side reports pc2's pings to pc1
time out, while everything else there works. What's wrong?

injection.action: point pc1's default route at a nonexistent gateway (.254)
injection.command: ip route replace default via 195.11.14.254 dev eth0

scenario.ground_truth:
Affected component: pc1 default route / gateway configuration
Mechanism: pc1's default route points at 195.11.14.254, an address
  that exists on no device (the real gateway is router1's eth1 at
  195.11.14.1). ARP for .254 gets no answer, so every off-subnet
  packet from pc1 dies locally with "Destination Host Unreachable".
  On-subnet traffic (the connected 195.11.14.0/24 route) still
  works, which is why pc1 can ping 195.11.14.1. The network side
  is fully healthy: router1 still advertises 195.11.14.0/24, the
  eBGP session is Established, and pc2's pings ARE delivered to
  pc1 -- but pc1's replies chase the phantom gateway and are never
  sent, so pc2 sees timeouts.
Localization: pc1
Root cause: pc1's default route points at nonexistent gateway
  195.11.14.254 instead of 195.11.14.1
Fix: `ip route replace default via 195.11.14.1 dev eth0` on pc1
scenario.fix_spec:
Restore pc1's default route -- `ip route replace default via 195.11.14.1 dev
eth0` on pc1. Off-subnet connectivity returns immediately; no router or BGP
change is needed.
scoring_axes: must-identify-component: default route / gateway points at nonexistent 195.11.14.254 instead of 195.11.14.1
bonus-exonerates-network: verifies the routers, the eBGP session and the advertised prefixes are healthy -- the fault is confined to pc1's own routing table

agent.diagnosis_text:
The fault is an incorrect default gateway configured on pc1. pc1's routing
table shows "default via 195.11.14.254 dev eth0", but router1's actual IP on
the pc1-facing interface (eth1) is 195.11.14.1/24 — the address 195.11.14.254
does not exist anywhere in the topology.

This perfectly explains every observed symptom. When pc1 pings its gateway
195.11.14.1, no default route is involved: the kernel's directly-connected
route for 195.11.14.0/24 delivers the ARP and ICMP packet in-subnet, so the
ping succeeds without touching the default route. When pc1 tries to reach
200.1.1.2 (or any off-subnet destination), the kernel forwards the packet to
the default gateway 195.11.14.254, ARPs for it, receives no reply, and
immediately returns "Destination Host Unreachable" to the application — exactly
the reported error. When pc2 pings pc1, the BGP-learned route on router2
(195.11.14.0/24 via 193.10.11.1) delivers the packet to pc1 successfully, but
pc1's echo reply is again dropped at the wrong gateway, so pc2 sees the ping
time out. The routers and BGP session are completely healthy: router1 and
router2 both have full, symmetric routing tables with correctly learned
prefixes.

Root cause: pc1's default gateway was set to 195.11.14.254 (likely a typo
during the "network settings cleanup") instead of the correct value 195.11.14.1.

Corrective fix: On pc1, replace the broken default route:
  ip route del default
  ip route add default via 195.11.14.1
Also update /etc/network/interfaces (or the lab startup script) so the correct
gateway 195.11.14.1 is configured persistently.

per_axis.rationale: The agent explicitly identifies pc1 as the faulty device with an incorrect default gateway configuration.

per_axis.rationale: The diagnosis explicitly says the routers and eBGP session are healthy and that BGP-learned prefixes reach pc1, confining the fault to pc1's routing table.
Correct remediation: restore pc1's default route to via 195.11.14.1 (the agent's ip route del/add and updating persistent config matches the expected fix).

The agent's logs explicitly show pc1's default route pointing at 195.11.14.254 and pc1's on-link address 195.11.14.2; the agent also ran router checks and reported router1's LAN address as 195.11.14.1 and healthy BGP. The inference that a wrong/nonexistent default gateway on pc1 causes the observed off-subnet failures is logically consistent and the writeup ties observed facts to the root cause and fix.
